title: Among joint-act adorers: some send only the exterior sign to the image; others the interior submission too—latria/dulia/hyperdulia debate
source_text: X. Rursus qui censent uno & eodem adorationis actu imaginem & exemplar simul posse & debere coli, in eo inter se dissentiunt; quod quidam id solum quod est in adoratione externum, ad imaginem referri & terminari existimant, internum vero cordis motum referendum esse ad solum exemplar: At vero plures alii contendunt imaginem cum exemplari simul adorari posse, non tantum eodem actu adorationis externo, sed etiam eadem interiori mentis subjectione, ut latius expositum fuit thesibus superioribus. In quibus etiam ostensum, cultum qui defertur imagini, juxta multorum sententiam, ejusdem esse generis & rationis cum eo qui defertur exemplari; ita ut imagines Christi latria colendae sint, Sanctorum vero dulia, Beatae autem Mariae Virginis hyperdulia: juxta alios vero cultum qui proprie & per se imaginibus exhibetur alterius esse generis & ordinis inferioris, quam cultum exemplaris ipsius; sed tamen analogice ad eum referri & reduci.
pass_a_gloss: Again, those who judge that by one and the same act of adoration image and exemplar together can and ought to be cultivated differ among themselves in this; that some think that only what is exterior in the adoration is referred and terminated to the image, but that the interior motion of the heart is to be referred to the exemplar alone: But indeed many others contend that the image can be adored together with the exemplar, not only by the same exterior act of adoration, but also by the same interior subjection of the mind, as was more largely set forth in the superior theses. In which it was also shown that the cult which is paid to the image, according to the opinion of many, is of the same genus and reason with that which is paid to the exemplar; so that the images of Christ are to be cultivated with latria, but those of the Saints with dulia, and those of the Blessed Virgin Mary with hyperdulia: but according to others the cult which is properly and per se exhibited to images is of another genus and of an inferior order than the cult of the exemplar itself; yet is nevertheless analogically referred and reduced to it.
pass_b_english: Joint-act camp still splits: Vasquez-style exterior-only toward the image vs interior submission aimed at both.
Many then assign latria/dulia/hyperdulia to Christ’s, saints’, and Mary’s images; others keep image-cult a lower, analogical order.

lemmas.gloss: by interior subjection of the mind

choices.why: Rival reduction of image-cult to exemplar-cult.
